page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-64 is a balanced, general-purpose compute instance based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon processor architecture. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.8 GHz, the instance delivers 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with hyperthreading. Cache architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 33 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 256 GB of system memory, providing a standard 4.0 GB of memory per vCPU. Hardware features include support for AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic AES extensions. The configuration bundles no integrated local SSD storage, relying exclusively on remote persistent disk options, and features zero GPU accelerators.

Benchmark assessments establish the n2-standard-64 as a reliable multi-core performer with pronounced strengths in memory-intensive operations. In PassMark testing, it achieves strong results in database operations (22,557.31) and extended instruction execution (52,398.44), supported by an overall PassMark CPU score of 46,235.74. Geekbench testing reflects solid multi-core throughput of 14,944.0, highlighted by strong Clang software compilation scores reaching 40,304.0. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth is a notable strength, recording 268.78 GB/sec in read tests and 131.67 GB/sec in write tests. Redis operations sustain approximately 55.0 million set operations per second, while static web throughput reaches 36.8 GB/sec. Conversely, large language model generation on 70B parameter models falls into the lower performance quartile at 2.67 tokens per second due to the lack of hardware accelerators.

From an operational cost perspective, the instance provides balanced resource density by avoiding the premium associated with GPU attachments or fast local NVMe drives. While workloads requiring extreme low-latency local I/O will face network storage overhead, the dedicated 64 vCPUs and strong memory throughput yield dependable CPU capacity for compute-dense workloads. The n2-standard-64 is well suited for enterprise database management systems, continuous integration build clusters, batch compilation pipelines, and containerized backend web infrastructure.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-64 is a balanced, general-purpose virtual machine powered by 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon x86_64 processors. Configured with 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores and 256 GB of system RAM, it maintains a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The instance includes AVX-512 and VNNI vector instruction sets but provides no bundled local storage or GPU acceleration, requiring network-attached block volumes for persistence. Benchmark results show solid performance across multi-core computing workloads, with upper-quartile execution in PassMark database operations, Clang software compilation, and uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidth. However, large-scale language model inference demonstrates weak throughput due to the absence of dedicated matrix accelerators. Offering dedicated CPU allocation and reliable throughput, this configuration provides cost-effective efficiency for multi-threaded build systems, medium-to-large relational databases, and enterprise backend application services.
